judge_verdict.summary: The agent shipped a correct merge_ordered fast path with large baseline speedups, but verifier scoring shows it is slower than the reference commit and below the 1.20× pass threshold.

verdict.outcome_rationale: This is a genuine agent-fault failure where the verifier's FAIL is correct. The GSO verifier reported binary_reward 0 with a continuous gm_speedup_patch_commit score of 0.643, below the 1.20 pass threshold and with opt_commit false [1][2][3][4]. The task asked the agent to optimize pandas merge_ordered performance while preserving functional equivalence and pursuing the best possible speedup [5]. The agent added a `_maybe_get_sorted_unique_inner_result` fast path in `pandas/core/reshape/merge.py` that uses `np.searchsorted` for inner merges on a single sorted unique key [6], reinstalled pandas, and declared success after seeing roughly 40× improvement on the provided benchmark versus the unpatched base (~0.27s to ~0.006s) plus 20 passing merge_ordered unit tests [7]. The hidden verifier confirmed correctness—all 20 benchmark scripts passed equivalence checks after the patch [8]—but measured the patch against a known upstream optimization at commit 061c2e9 and found the agent slower on the headline case (test 0 mean ~0.007s patch vs ~0.004s commit) and ~0.64× on the geometric-mean commit/patch metric overall [9][4]. The agent never had access to that reference commit or the held-out 20-test suite, and its self-checks were limited to the single instruction benchmark and installed unit tests, so it concluded success without meeting the task's performance bar [7][8]. Because correctness was preserved but required speed relative to the reference solution was not achieved, this is TN, not FN.
